mcqs.learning_point: चित्र और पाठ के संबंध को समझना
mcqs.question: In the illustration that accompanies the story "फटे जूते", a pair of torn shoes is shown beside a polished shoe rack. How does this picture relate to the text?

options.A: It highlights the contrast between poverty and wealth, reflecting the satire on external appearance.
options.B: It shows the protagonist’s desire to own new shoes.
options.C: It depicts a literal event described in the story.
options.D: It is an unrelated decorative element.

mcqs.answer: It highlights the contrast between poverty and wealth, reflecting the satire on external appearance.
mcqs.explanation: The picture is deliberately placed to underline the story’s central satire – the difference between outward show (polished shoes) and the real condition of the poor (torn shoes). This visual‑text link reinforces Premchand’s critique of judging by appearance. Options B, C and D either add a meaning not present in the text or ignore the satirical purpose.

mcqs.learning_point: पाठ के निहित सामाजिक संदेश को समझना
mcqs.question: A student observes a classmate wearing brand‑new shoes while another student walks barefoot. Which social message from Premchand’s "फटे जूते" is most relevant to this situation?

options.A: We should share our wealth with those who have less.
options.B: One should not judge a person solely by his outward appearance.
options.C: Buying expensive items is a sign of success.
options.D: Material prosperity is the ultimate goal in life.

mcqs.answer: One should not judge a person solely by his outward appearance.
mcqs.explanation: The story’s hidden social message warns against superficial judgments based on how a person looks or what he wears. Option B captures this idea. Option A, while noble, is not the core message; C and D contradict the satirical tone of the story.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about satire (व्यंग्य) is a common misconception?

options.A: Satire always uses humor only to make the audience laugh without any serious purpose.
options.B: Satire often employs irony to expose social flaws.
options.C: Satire can be both humorous and critical at the same time.
options.D: Satire aims to provoke thought about societal issues.

mcqs.answer: Satire always uses humor only to make the audience laugh without any serious purpose.
mcqs.explanation: Satire is not merely for laughter; its primary aim is to criticize and provoke reflection on societal problems. Options B, C and D correctly describe satire’s characteristics, while A incorrectly reduces it to pure entertainment.

mcqs.learning_point: प्रेमचंद के व्यक्तित्व के संदर्भ को समझना
mcqs.question: Considering Premchand’s lifelong concern for the downtrodden, which reasoning best explains his use of satire in "फटे जूते"?

options.A: To mock the poor for their lack of material possessions.
options.B: To highlight the hypocrisy of judging people by their outward appearance.
options.C: To promote a luxurious lifestyle as the ideal.
options.D: To entertain readers without delivering any deeper message.

mcqs.answer: To highlight the hypocrisy of judging people by their outward appearance.
mcqs.explanation: Premchand’s personal empathy for the marginalized drives him to expose societal hypocrisy through satire. Option B aligns with his intent. Options A and C contradict his humanitarian outlook, and D ignores the purposeful social critique embedded in the story.

mcqs.learning_point: सादगी और दिखावे के अंतर को समझना
mcqs.question: How does Premchand differentiate between ‘सादगी’ (simplicity) and ‘दिखावा’ (show) in "फटे जूते"?

options.A: सादगी refers to inner honesty, whereas दिखावा denotes outward pretence.
options.B: Both terms convey the same meaning of modest living.
options.C: सादगी is associated with wealth, while दिखावा is linked to poverty.
options.D: दिखावा represents truthfulness, while सादगी indicates falsehood.

mcqs.answer: सादगी refers to inner honesty, whereas दिखावा denotes outward pretence.
mcqs.explanation: Premchand uses ‘सादगी’ to praise genuine modesty and moral integrity, while ‘दिखावा’ criticises superficial display of status. Options B, C and D invert or conflate the meanings, which is contrary to the author’s distinction.

mcqs.learning_point: लेखक के व्यंग्यात्मक दृष्टिकोण को पहचानना
mcqs.question: Which line from "फटे जूते" best illustrates Premchand’s satirical viewpoint on society?

options.A: ‘जैसे ही जूते फटे, लोग भी फटे हुए दिखते हैं’
options.B: ‘सच्ची खुशी तो सादगी में ही मिलती है’
options.D: ‘बच्चे खेलते हैं, परन्तु उनके जूते नहीं होते’

mcqs.answer: ‘जैसे ही जूते फटे, लोग भी फटे हुए दिखते हैं’
mcqs.explanation: Option A uses a direct comparison between torn shoes and the ‘torn’ (degraded) moral state of people, embodying Premchand’s satirical critique of judging by external signs. Options B and D convey moral ideas but lack the sharp satirical edge, while C is a factual statement without satire.

mcqs.learning_point: चित्र और पाठ के संबंध को समझना
mcqs.question: What is the primary relationship between the picture and the text in "फटे जूते"?

options.A: They are complementary, showing the contrast between appearance and reality.
options.B: The picture repeats the same information already given in the text.
options.C: The picture contradicts the main idea of the text.
options.D: There is no meaningful connection; the picture is decorative.

mcqs.answer: They are complementary, showing the contrast between appearance and reality.
mcqs.explanation: The illustration is deliberately chosen to reinforce the story’s theme of external show versus inner reality, making it complementary. Options B and C misinterpret the purpose, and D ignores the intentional link.

mcqs.learning_point: पाठ के निहित सामाजिक संदेश को समझना
mcqs.question: What is the underlying social message of Premchand’s "फटे जूते"?

options.A: Do not judge a person solely by his outward appearance.
options.B: Acquire the latest fashion to gain respect.
options.C: Wealth is the ultimate measure of a person’s worth.

mcqs.answer: Do not judge a person solely by his outward appearance.
mcqs.explanation: The story uses satire to convey that external markers like shoes do not reflect a person’s true value. Options B, C and D promote materialism, which is opposite to the author’s intended message.
